drivingQuestion: Does the mishna permit men to watch the sota or only women?
outcomeNote: resolved by Abaye and Rava in the next unit (sotah.sugya043)

segments.he: וְכׇל הָרוֹצֶה לִרְאוֹת בָּהּ יִרְאֶה וְכוּ׳. הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא. אָמְרַתְּ: כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִרְאוֹת בָּהּ רוֹאֶה, אַלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא גַּבְרֵי וְלָא שְׁנָא נְשֵׁי, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים מוּתָּרוֹת לִרְאוֹתָהּ: נָשִׁים — אִין, אֲנָשִׁים — לָא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And anyone who desires to watch her may watch,» except for her slaves and maidservants, who are not permitted to watch because her heart is emboldened by them. And all of the women are permitted to watch her. The Gemara comments: «This» matter «is itself difficult,» as there is an internal contradiction in the mishna. First «you say: And anyone who desires to watch her may watch. Apparently,» there «is no difference» whether the onlookers are «men and» there «is no difference» whether they are «women;» all are permitted to observe the rite. «And then» the mishna «teaches: And all of the women are permitted to watch her,» which indicates «women, yes,» they may watch her, but «men, no,» they may not.
